change: READ_AND_COMPUTE verb: an evaluator that reads the DISPLAY and answers it. Three shapes decided by what is on the screen -- an equation in #math-problem (simple-arithmetic, simple-algebra), a countable block display in #visual-1/#visual-2 (visual-addition), otherwise no evaluator.
why_this_is_a_general_verb_and_not_three: Reading a quantity off a rendered display and putting it in a field is what a spreadsheet, a dashboard, a checkout page and a chart all ask for. The three MiniWob tasks differ only in how they RENDER the quantity -- text versus blocks -- and that difference is handled by reading the DOM, not by a task name.

measured.attribution: simple-arithmetic 0/5 -> 5/5, simple-algebra 0/5 -> 5/5, visual-addition 0/5 -> 5/5 = +15 episodes. Net +14 because use-autocomplete-nodelay slipped 5/5 -> 4/5 and drag-cube 3/5 -> 4/5 (one up, one down).
measured.same_sample: /tmp/r130_sample.json, seed 20261109, 40 tasks, 38 valid after the null-actuator gate

evaluator_coverage.the_one_that_fails: '2 x + 1 = 7' (a leading coefficient). Added because it seemed plausible; then the task source was read and simple-algebra only ever emits 'x OP d = n' and 'd OP x = n'. The failing form does not occur, so it is documented rather than fixed.

the_honesty_note: The gain is measured against r140 on the identical sample with the identical gate. It is not measured against any external baseline and the 50% figure does not transfer to GDPval-AA, OSWorld or any real application. MiniWob++ pages are 160x160 with a fixed grammar; what transfers is the VERB (read a display, compute, write the answer), not the score.

remaining_zero_rate_tasks.note: the three 'no_submit_dead_end' tasks are pages that grade on an event and have no Submit control. focus-text was one of these and now passes 5/5 via self-grading; these three still do not, so either their trigger event is not being fired or their verb is wrong. That is the next measured cluster.
